question: Can PaperTeam reduce academically worthless cross-section repetition in Chinese surveys by organising evidence, section tasks and length — while keeping every key scientific fact and without raising model cost?

stages.1_evaluator: classification layer on top of the frozen lexical detector (backend/src/review/academicRedundancyClassifier.ts): M / L / P / S / X / E / F / uncertain with explicit rules R1–R9, two metrics (A lexical restated share; B harmful share with lower / upper bound). Calibrated on the M13.7.8 outputs (development set); M13.7.8 is NOT re-judged — its pre-registered gate was metric A and stays FAIL.
stages.2_B2: minimal revision of Arm B's task block only (argumentUnitsV2): no rendered「见 X 一节」pointers, one behavioural cross-section policy, synthesis-style compare task, conclude task with '不写指向其他章节的句子'. Evidence partition, upper-bound lengths (180/400/400/320/160), lengthPolicy, lengthInstructionReplace and the production buildSectionPrompt are unchanged from M13.7.8 Arm B.
stages.3_dev: B2 once on the M13.7.8 SimCLR topic (development set, 5 tasks) against the frozen A / B outputs; one evidence-based task-block correction allowed with all failed outputs kept — none was needed.
stages.4_heldout: two new topics, A and B2 each, five sections, independent sessions per arm (20 tasks)
stages.5_attribution: H3-only (task-only arm: baseline evidence + baseline length + B2 task block without lengthPolicy) once, five sections, on ONE held-out topic selected by the rule below

heldout.topic: 大语言模型偏好对齐方法综述：人类反馈强化学习、直接偏好优化与 AI 反馈
heldout.argumentStructure: reference pipeline → two cost-reduction routes (remove the RL stage / replace human labels) → synthesis along four dimensions; mostly qualitative claims with a few numbers (1.3B vs 175B, 100x)
heldout.evidence: 10 direct + 2 partial negative controls (E11 DPO universal superiority; E12 no human involvement at all)

heldout.topic: 超导量子纠错实验综述：表面码规模扩展与突破盈亏平衡的逻辑量子比特
heldout.argumentStructure: two experimental routes answering different questions (scaling with distance vs beating break-even); numerically dense (≥ 12 must-retain numbers) with metrics that are not commensurable across routes
heldout.evidence: 10 direct + 2 partial negative controls (E11 requirements already reached; E12 G and lifetime factor are the same metric)

independence: neither topic, paper set nor outline was used by M13.7.2–M13.7.8 (Transformer, DPR/RAG, LoRA/QLoRA, FedAvg/SCAFFOLD, SimCLR/MoCo/BYOL/SimSiam); `rg` over scripts/, docs/, backend/src, backend/test for the paper ids, titles and key terms returned nothing before the fixtures were written

sources.retrieval: public arXiv abstract pages fetched 2026-10-12 (HTTP 200 direct); <meta name=citation_abstract> decoded; raw HTML + SHA256 kept privately, decoded abstracts public in sources-abstracts-*.json
sources.verificationLevel: abstract — every quote asserted to be an exact substring of the decoded abstract by the fixture builder before freeze; NOT full-text grounding, NOT a production Grounding / Judge verdict

runtime: PiRuntimeAdapter, production buildSectionPrompt, toolPolicy read_only, 300 s per task, one shared writer session per arm (contextScope writing/acceptance/<arm>/sections), arms in independent projects / sessions; PROJECTS_ROOT outside the repository

budget.taskUnit: one runtime.runAgent call = one Writer task (one section)
budget.requestUnit: assistant turns reported by PiRuntimeAdapter usage = underlying provider requests; recorded separately per task; 30 tasks does NOT imply ≤ 30 requests
budget.ledger: single budget file D:/PaperTeamData/M13_7_9/model-budget.json (--budget-file, --max-tasks 30) shared by every arm of the round; one reservation per task before dispatch
budget.retryPolicy: a task may be retried inside the budget only for a clear configuration error; the failed record is kept and reported; no retries for unfavorable content; no automatic extension beyond 30

arms.input: production buildSectionPrompt: full 12-record evidence snapshot to every section, 约350字 per section, original keyPoints task

per-section evidence partition (argumentUnitsV2.evidenceIds) + per-section upper-bound length (180/400/400/320/160, lengthPolicy) + B2 task block (role label / task / doNotExplain concepts without pointers / crossSectionPolicy)

full 12-record snapshot + 约350字 + original instructions (as baseline) + B2 task block WITHOUT the lengthPolicy line; isolates H3 (argument task + negative scope) from H1 (evidence partition) and H2 (length)

order: freeze → commit → alignment A → alignment B2 → qec A → qec B2 → evaluate both → H3-only on the topic selected by `h3SelectionRule` → evaluate; no additional arms, seeds or prompt tuning
h3SelectionRule: run task-only on the held-out topic whose Baseline shows the HIGHER metric-B lower-bound harmful share (depends only on the two Baseline outputs, not on any treatment output); tie → alignment. If both Baselines are below the discriminative floor, still run it on alignment and report the arm as low-discrimination.

evaluation.frozenBefore: first provider request on a held-out fixture; classifier rules / thresholds, detector, markers, mustRetain, fixtures, runner and evaluation scripts are not edited afterwards (if a marker misses a legitimate spelling, both the marker count and the manual count are reported — the marker is NOT widened). A technical bug found after the freeze keeps the frozen numbers as the gate figures; the fixed figures are a supplementary report only.
evaluation.detector: analyzeCrossSectionRedundancy defaults (minSentenceChars 12, minShared 6, containment ≥ 0.5, jaccard ≥ 0.2); the LIMITATION_PATTERNS extension of this round only affects limitation statistics and the L rule, never pairs or metric A

classifier.roles: explicit from argumentUnitsV2.sections[*].role (framing / develop / develop / compare / conclude)
classifier.rules: R2 L → R1 S → R3 F → R5 transition → R4 P → R6 M → R7 X (R7v verbatim, R7u grey) → R8 E (R8v verbatim, R8m enumeration) → R9; see ACADEMIC_REDUNDANCY_RULES

evaluation.metricB: harmful share = chars of sentences flagged harmful (M / L / P / S / verbatim X / verbatim E; attributed to the harmful side, deduplicated per sentence) / all sentence chars; lower bound excludes uncertain, upper bound includes it; isolated develop-section limitation sentences are uncertain, never harmful
evaluation.discriminativeFloor: a Baseline with fewer than 3 harmful sentences or a metric-B lower bound below 5 % is marked 'low discrimination for de-duplication'; on such a topic the de-duplication percentage is reported but NOT used as a pass criterion — completeness and newly introduced defects are evaluated first

gate.perTopic: B2.harmfulShareLower ≤ 0.70 × A.harmfulShareLower (≥ 30 % relative drop) on topics above the discriminative floor AND mustRetain checklist fully present AND no unknown cite key AND no new quote-exceeding factual claim that A does not also have AND no negative-control escalation AND no section that skips its task by writing short
gate.note: 30 % is a pre-registered engineering screen, not proof of generalisation; shorter text alone is never counted as improvement; metric A, absolute harmful chars, sentence chars, signpost count (non-framing) and verbatim-carry count are reported next to it

verdictRules.PASS: both held-out topics (or the one above the floor, with the other clean on completeness / defects) meet the per-topic gate; signposts and verbatim comparison carries are no longer a main defect; cost not up without benefit
verdictRules.PARTIAL: improvement on one topic but not the other, or evaluator unable to separate harmful from necessary repetition, or any must-retain loss / fact risk / insufficient sample
verdictRules.FAIL: no effective improvement, or important fact loss, or clear increase of quote-exceeding mechanism claims, or a severe regression

priorityOrder: 2 no new quote-exceeding mechanism or strong conclusion
5 signposts / verbatim comparison carries not a new main defect
6 cost and latency not up without benefit

manualReading.harmfulRestatement: a sentence that re-explains a mechanism / result already fully explained in its owner section without adding the current section's own analysis; introduction scope summaries, half-sentence reminders, comparison-axis reminders that end in a contrastive conclusion, and conclusion echoes are NOT counted; signpost sentences outside the introduction ARE counted
manualReading.factAudit: every mechanism / result sentence with a cite is checked against the quote of the cited source; flags: partial-only support, uncovered technical detail, widened performance claim, inference written as fact, unverified claim kept behind a disclaimer; counts for A and B2 are compared — B2 must not add flags that A does not have
manualReading.shortWriteAvoidance: a section fails its task if a mustRetain item for that section is missing or if a comparison dimension listed in the task is not addressed
manualReading.classifierAudit: every classifier verdict on held-out outputs is read; disagreements are recorded per pair (class by rules vs class by reading) and reported as an agreement rate — the rules are NOT edited

introduction: scope: aligning LLMs with user intent / human preferences; RLHF as reference pipeline; two cost-reduction routes (direct preference optimisation; AI feedback replacing human labels)
no own experiments / four abstracts as material
human: motivation: bigger models not inherently better at following intent; untruthful / toxic / unhelpful outputs
InstructGPT pipeline: labeler demonstrations → supervised fine-tuning of GPT-3 → rankings of outputs → RL from human feedback
1.3B InstructGPT outputs preferred to 175B GPT-3 despite 100x fewer parameters (human evaluations on their prompt distribution)
improvements in truthfulness, reductions in toxic output, minimal regressions on public NLP datasets; still makes simple mistakes
RLHF complex / unstable: fit reward model, then RL fine-tuning without drifting too far

DPO: reparameterisation of the reward model → optimal policy in closed form → simple classification loss; stable, performant, lightweight; no sampling during fine-tuning, no significant hyperparameter tuning

DPO results as scoped: as well as or better than existing methods; exceeds PPO-based RLHF in sentiment control; matches or improves summarisation and single-turn dialogue; simpler to implement and train
aifeedback: Constitutional AI: no human labels identifying harmful outputs; only human oversight = list of rules / principles
SL phase: sample initial model → self-critiques and revisions → fine-tune on revised responses
RL phase: sample fine-tuned model → model judges which of two samples is better → preference model from AI preferences → RL with it as reward (RLAIF)
result: harmless but non-evasive assistant that explains its objections
RLAIF (Lee et al.): reward model trained on preferences from an off-the-shelf LLM; comparable to RLHF on summarisation, helpful dialogue, harmless dialogue
RLAIF outperforms SFT baseline even when the AI labeler is the same size as the policy or the same checkpoint
d-RLAIF obtains rewards directly from an off-the-shelf LLM during RL, bypassing RM training; superior to canonical RLAIF
comparison: dimension: explicit reward model fitted or not
dimension: RL stage needed or not
dimension: feedback source (human labels / principles / off-the-shelf model)
dimension: evaluation task scope of each paper
limitation: no own experiments, four abstracts only
limitation: results from different models / tasks / settings → no performance ranking
partials E11 / E12 not written as fact
conclusion: relation of the reference pipeline and the two routes, and what each changes
unified evaluation as future work, not completed contribution

introduction: scope: superconducting QEC experiments; two routes (surface-code scaling with distance; single logical qubits beating break-even)
no own experiments / four abstracts as material
surface: principle: more physical qubits enhance protection but add error sources; error density must be low enough for logical performance to improve with code size
distance-5 modestly outperforms ensemble of distance-3: 2.914%±0.016% vs 3.028%±0.023% logical error per cycle (and over 25 cycles)
distance-25 repetition code: 1.7×10^-6 logical error per round floor set by a single high-energy event (1.6×10^-7 excluding it)
first experimental demonstration where QEC begins to improve with increasing qubit number
below threshold: distance-7 code and distance-5 code with real-time decoder
Λ = 2.14±0.02 suppression when increasing distance by two; 101-qubit distance-7 code 0.143%±0.003% per cycle
beyond break-even: 2.4±0.3 × best physical qubit lifetime
real-time decoding: average latency 63 µs at distance-5 up to a million cycles; cycle time 1.1 µs
repetition codes up to distance-29 limited by rare correlated error events ~once per hour / 3×10^9 cycles
'if scaled, could realize' operational requirements — stated as potential, not achieved
breakeven: previous attempts overwhelmed by excess errors; whether QEC can extend coherence was an open question
fully stabilised, error-corrected logical qubit whose coherence exceeds every imperfect component; coherence gain G = 2.27±0.07
achieved by superconducting circuit fabrication + model-free reinforcement learning (among other domains)
discrete-variable encodings (e.g. photon numbers) make codewords orthogonal; previous repetitive QEC demos stayed below the break-even point (logical lifetime shorter than best physical qubit)
logical qubit in photon-number states of a microwave cavity, dispersively coupled to an ancilla superconducting qubit
pulse with tailored frequency comb on the ancilla → repetitive high-fidelity syndrome extraction + feedback correction
exceeds break-even by about 16% lifetime enhancement
comparison: dimension: metric definitions (per-cycle logical error / Λ / lifetime factor vs coherence gain / lifetime enhancement %) → not directly comparable
dimension: limiting error sources (rare correlated events; imperfect components)
limitation: no own experiments, four abstracts only
limitation: different metrics / platforms / settings → no performance ranking
partials E11 / E12 not written as fact
conclusion: what each route answers (improvement with scale vs beating break-even) and their relation
unified-metric comparison as future work, not completed contribution

alignment: DPO outperforms RLHF on all / every task (E11 partial)
AI feedback needs no human involvement / oversight at all (E12 partial)
any PPO / KL / β coefficient, dataset sizes, label counts, model sizes beyond 1.3B / 175B, win rates, specific principles text, number of principles
RLAIF (Lee et al.) attributed to Constitutional AI's authors or vice versa
qec: surface code already meets fault-tolerance requirements (E11 partial)
G = 2.27 and 2.4× lifetime treated as the same metric or ranked against each other (E12 partial)
calling the Sivak et al. encoding GKP / bosonic / cat (not in the quotes)
any threshold value, physical error rate, qubit count other than 101, number of cycles other than 25 / a million, decoder name, Λ for other distances
attributing the 16% result to the Google device or Λ to the cavity experiment

designLimits: single sample, single sampling run per arm; GLM outputs are not deterministic; no claim of stable generalisation; no multi-seed sweep (not authorised this round)
H3-only is one arm on one topic: directional attribution only, not causal decomposition; no full three-factor design

the classifier is lexical + positional: it cannot see paraphrased re-explanation that shares < 6 tokens, nor an introduction that pre-expands a mechanism in words the owner section does not reuse; concept markers and reading cover that gap
roles are given by the fixture, not inferred by a production Planner; Planner reliability for role / evidenceIds / doNotExplain is out of scope
evidence is abstract-level; fact audit compares sentences to abstract quotes, not to full texts

the alignment topic may carry little baseline redundancy (qualitative claims spread across four papers); if its Baseline is below the discriminative floor the topic is evaluated on completeness and defects, not on the percentage
noTuning: no prompt, fixture, marker, threshold, classifier rule, runner or evaluation-script edit after the first held-out request; unfavorable outputs retained; no selection among samples; dev-stage refinements of the classifier (R2u, R5 transitions, R8m enumeration criteria, limitation sentinel extension) are recorded in the report with before / after numbers on every arm
